title: Put two windows side by side
summary: Use the Windows key with the arrow keys and Snap Assist to arrange two windows.

steps.say: Open two apps you use, for example a browser and File Explorer. Say done when both are open.
hints: Press the Windows key and E to open File Explorer as one of them.
Open apps from Start by typing their name and pressing Enter.
steps.why: Snapping needs at least two windows to fill both halves.

steps.say: Click the title bar of the window you want on the left.
hints: The title bar is the strip at the very top of the window.
Press Alt and Tab to bring the window you want to the front.
steps.why: Snap shortcuts act on the window in front.

steps.say: Hold the Windows key and press the left arrow.

checks.prompt: Does one window now fill the left half of the screen?

hints: The window jumps to the left half and thumbnails of other windows appear on the right.
Drag the window by its title bar to the left edge of the screen until an outline appears.
steps.why: Half-screen windows let you read one thing while working in another.

steps.say: Click the other window in the thumbnails on the right side.

check.prompt: Are two windows now side by side, each filling one half of the screen?

hints: These thumbnails are Snap Assist. Pick the window you want on the right.
If the thumbnails went away, click the other window and press the Windows key and the right arrow.
steps.why: Snap Assist fills the empty half in one click.

steps.say: Hover over the maximize button of either window to see more layouts.
hints: The maximize button is the square, second from the right at the top right corner.
Press the Windows key and Z to open the same layouts with the keyboard.
steps.why: Snap layouts offer thirds and quarters for bigger screens.

steps.say: To make a window full screen again, click it and press the Windows key and the up arrow.

checks.prompt: Is one window now maximized to fill the whole screen?

hints: The up arrow maximizes, the down arrow restores the previous size.
Double-click the window's title bar to maximize it.
steps.why: Knowing how to undo a layout makes snapping stress free.
